_meta.description: Machine-readable component map. Read before exploring the codebase. Update as part of every feature branch that adds or moves components.
_meta.upstream_debt_legend: Files/dirs still using HestiaCP-specific paths (/usr/local/hestia, /etc/hestiacp, hestia-nginx, hestia-php) that need migration to HestiaRE conventions.
_meta.os_targets: All four are first-class, equal-priority: debian-bookworm (12), debian-trixie (13), ubuntu-noble (24.04), ubuntu-26lts (26.04). load_os_profile (func/helper.sh) is the single source for OS_ID/CODENAME/RELEASE/EXIM_USR/BASE_PKGS_EXTRA. Every feature must work on all four; verify on the VM fleet before a PR.
_meta.distro_quirks: Cross-cutting gotchas that bite more than one service (grep these before assuming a service failure is your bug): (1) Ubuntu 26.04 ships ENFORCED AppArmor profiles that deny access other distros allow — proftpd can't read the panel cert under /usr/local/hestia/ssl (h-add-sys-proftpd drops share/proftpd/apparmor-local into the profile's local/ hook), and mariadbd's profile denies the dac_override the mariadb-install-db bootstrap needs (h-add-sys-mariadb unloads it for the init, reloads after). Suspect AppArmor on any 'Permission denied as root' on ub26. (2) Package names/splits differ by distro+version: proftpd-basic is bookworm-only (else proftpd-core), and modern proftpd (1.3.9 / 1.3.8 on trixie+ubuntu) moved mod_tls into proftpd-mod-crypto — omitting it silently disables FTPS. libzip is libzip4t64 on ub24 (t64 transition) but libzip5 on ub26. (3) apt-cache/apt-get output is localized — always LC_ALL=C before grepping for 'Candidate:' etc. (4) dovecot 2.3 (deb12) vs 2.4 (deb13/ub26) need version-split configs (share/dovecot/{2.3,2.4}/).
_meta.reference_docs: CLAUDE.md (rules), this map (component->files), PATHS.md (filesystem layout), and STRUCTURE.md (why the structure diverges from HestiaCP and what each divergence forces - read it before assuming why a subsystem was rebuilt: panel Caddy/Sury, the system-user split, protected downloads, webmail loopback, the FileManager/SFTP-jail rebuilds, /etc/hestia, and the permanent removals). Keep STRUCTURE.md current in the same PR as any structural change. Per-folder PROVENANCE.json (bin/, web/, share/) tracks per-file upstream heritage + RAW churn divergence (triage only); complements VENDORED.json (third-party) and STRUCTURE.md; recompute is a manual, occasional job.

upstream_provenance.purpose: Maps HestiaRE files back to their HestiaCP origin so an upstream advisory or bugfix can be diffed/cherry-picked against the right file. Fork point: HestiaCP 1.9.6, kept read-only in the upstream/hestiacp branch. Each component carries an `upstream_ref` using these tags.

tags.near-verbatim: upstream file, renamed and/or path-migrated (v-*→h-*, /etc/hestiacp→/etc/hestia) but logic intact — cherry-pick candidate for isolated bugfixes
tags.reimplemented: clean HestiaRE reimplementation that diverges from upstream — do NOT cherry-pick, port by hand; the v-* symlink is usually removed (symlink_policy.escalation_rule)
tags.moved: upstream file relocated in-tree (mainly install/deb/* and install/common/* → share/*, #119) but otherwise near-verbatim
tags.removed: upstream component deleted from HestiaRE (bind9/DNS #58/#283, web terminal #59, REST API #146, SpamAssassin #284, software installer #56)
tags.hestiare-native: no upstream equivalent — HestiaRE-only (Caddy + hestia-php panel services, the pure-bash installer, panel Eigenbau libs, repo tooling)

upstream_provenance.cherry_pick_rule: Direct cherry-pick ONLY for verbatim/near-verbatim files carrying an isolated, dependency-free bugfix (CLAUDE.md). reimplemented/moved/native = port manually. Always verify installed==fixed against the actual file, never the version label (#386 method).
upstream_provenance.verification_note: The #386 triage is a worked example: near-verbatim files (func/db.sh) took a direct helper cherry-pick; reimplemented ones (func/main.sh parse_object_kv_list, the search-object commands) were confirmed safe/ported by hand, not cherry-picked.

drift_watch.purpose: Machine-checkable per-file drift markers (#412). share/upstream/sync-upstream.sh reads this map and, after refreshing the upstream/hestiacp snapshot, flags any listed file that upstream MOVED since its checked_ref — so drift is caught deterministically, not by chance (the jailbash 5-bind drift behind `--tmpfs /usr/share` was a lucky find). checked_ref is the upstream/hestiacp commit the HestiaRE copy was last human-verified against; bump it ONLY after re-verifying the file against the newer upstream. upstream_path handles renames (v-*→h-*). A ref-stamp (not a flat ignore list) distinguishes 'deliberately diverged, verified at ref X' from 'not looked at yet'.

cli_commands.description: All CLI commands. h-* prefix is HestiaRE-native (renamed from v-* in Issue #22). v-* symlinks for HestiaCP compatibility added in Issue #23. No hl-* commands.

symlink_policy.baseline: Each h-* command that predated Issue #23 has one v-* symlink. New h-* commands created after Issue #23 get NO v-* symlink — the v-* name never existed.
symlink_policy.escalation_rule: When a command is substantially rewritten and diverges significantly from its HestiaCP upstream equivalent, its v-* symlink is removed. Rationale: prevent accidental upstream cherry-picks onto an internally incompatible implementation. Applied in Issue #54 (v-add-sys-roundcube removed after total rewrite for OS-package migration).
symlink_policy.deletion: When removing an h-* command: remove its v-* symlink too — no orphans.
symlink_policy.creation: Committed v-* symlinks ship in the tarball, so the installer does NOT blanket-create them (a `for h-* ; ln -s v-*` loop minted an orphan alias for every HestiaRE-native command, #123). configure_hestia only prunes dangling v-* (a `find -xtype l` — e.g. an alias left pointing at a renamed/removed h-*); h-check-sys-smoke check_v_symlinks_resolve guards against a dangling alias at runtime. No allowlist: an extra working alias for a native command is harmless and not worth maintaining a list for a compat layer meant to fade out.

func_libraries.description: Shared bash function libraries sourced by all CLI commands and the installer. Core runtime dependency.

file_roles.main.sh: Core utilities: source_conf(), check_result(), output formatting, logging, JSON/shell serialization. Object parsing: parse_object_kv_list (PHP tokenizer, quote-safe, single eval — the upstream double-eval RCE GHSA-w3mx is NOT present, empirically verified #386) and parse_object_kv_list_non_eval (declare -g, no eval — use this for any user-controlled conf-field payload). Input hardening from the HestiaCP 1.9.8 adoption (#471): func/internal/sanitize_html.php (own dependency-free DOMDocument allow-list sanitizer for panel-rendered HTML - p/span/code/a/strong/br + safe href, drops script/on*/js:; used by h-add-user-notification since NOTICE renders via Alpine x-html), is_notification_topic/notice_valid (CR/LF + length guards on the single-line notifications.conf), and is_no_quote_format (blocks a single-quote/newline breaking out of a single-quoted field interpolated into the executed restore queue backup.pipe, GHSA-2xw3). SFTP jail membership helpers add_chroot_jail/delete_chroot_jail (#413: usermod -aG / gpasswd -d on the sftp-jailed group — the per-session jail itself is built by pam_namespace, see ssh_shell_jail.sftp_jail). manage_sshd_allowusers add|del <user> (#412): co-maintains the AllowUsers login allowlist in /etc/ssh/sshd_config for panel users — opt-in (acts only if an AllowUsers line exists; installer seeds one commented), edits ONLY the token whose base==user so operator entries (root@IP, maintenance) and the commented/active state survive, validates with `sshd -t` before swapping, reloads sshd only when active, re-comments rather than leaving an active line empty (lockout guard); called from h-add-user/h-delete-user AND rebuild_user (func/rebuild.sh) so restore/rebuild — which bypass h-add-user — re-add the user (else a restored user is missing from an active line and silently locked out).
file_roles.domain.sh: Domain validation and template checking for web and mail
file_roles.rebuild.sh: User and domain rebuild logic — regenerates service configs from HestiaRE data. Queue invariant: lines appended to conf/queue/*.pipe (run via `bash` by h-update-sys-queue) must contain only validated identifiers (username/domain), never free text (GHSA-47mf).
file_roles.syshealth.sh: System health monitoring, RRD graph generation, service status checks
file_roles.db.sh: MySQL/MariaDB and PostgreSQL connection helpers, host configuration. Passwords entering SQL MUST go through mysql_sql_escape()/sql_escape() before 'IDENTIFIED BY'/'PASSWORD' literals (GHSA-8w7m, #386); no eval in this file.
file_roles.backup.sh: Local, FTP, and Restic backup/restore handlers with retention logic
file_roles.ip.sh: IP address validation, RDNS checking, IPv4/IPv6 utilities
file_roles.docker.md: Per-user rootless Docker (#389). Host side: h-add-sys-docker / h-delete-sys-docker install docker-ce from the OFFICIAL repo (a scoped exception - neither Debian packages compose v2, the OS docker.io spans 20.10 to 29.1, and dockerd-rootless.sh ships only in Debian's build), disable the rootful daemon INCLUDING docker.socket (else socket activation resurrects it), and refuse on cgroup v1. Deliberately unpinned: no OS package shares a name with that repo. No cgroup delegation drop-in either - systemd already ships user@.service with Delegate=pids memory cpu on all four targets, and adding cpuset/io on the template would widen every session on the box. Customer side: h-add-user-docker creates the companion at uid-1000 with its OWN private group (the customer group would be caught by the customer home's group::--- ACL entry and never reach other::--x, so the companion could not traverse into its own home), writes the ORDER-SENSITIVE subuid/subgid triple that maps container 1000 to the customer, and starts the daemon with a group-owned socket in ~/.companion. Verified maps: 0->companion, 1000->customer. Traps: systemd-run --machine starts from a bare environment and the rootless setuptool refuses without HOME; the setuptool already starts the daemon, so its exit code is NOT the verdict and a later `enable --now` is a no-op; a restored home arrives with the unit enabled and the previous host's override, so its dead-socket start latches systemd's rate limiter and needs reset-failed. Liveness is proved by asking the API, never by [ -S ] on the socket file, which survives the daemon that made it. Backups exclude ~/.companion/.local/share/docker (images are pulled); h-restore-user re-owns the tree to the new companion uid BEFORE re-enabling, since tar cannot map it by name when the account does not exist yet.
file_roles.identity.sh: Panel user identity ALLOCATION (#388), not derivation. The username hash only picks where to start looking; the first free slot wins and stays that user's uid, as in classic HestiaCP. Interleaved 1000-blocks: customers in the odd thousands (11000-41999), each companion in the block below (10000-40999), 16000 slots, sub_base = 100000 + k*65536, disjoint by construction and below 2^31. A taken slot is not an error - identity_allocate reprobes with H(username:n). Backups carry NO authoritative identity and restores allocate fresh: portability comes from tar resolving ownership by NAME on extract (verified - a file archived as uid 5001 lands on 5099 once the name maps there), which is why the account is created BEFORE the unpack and why h-backup-user must never gain --numeric-owner. The only case still needing a chown is a restore under a different username, where tar finds no local name and falls back to the archived numbers; the inherited old_uid/new_uid re-chown in h-restore-user covers it. Paired with login_defs_guard (func/helper.sh), which caps UID_MAX/GID_MAX below the band and raises SUB_UID_MAX: the shipped default 600100000 sits below our highest range end (1048675999) and would otherwise reject roughly 43% of subordinate ranges.
file_roles.firewall.sh: Firewall renderer library - the ONE place that knows the backend's syntax. Renders the object model into a single nft `inet hestia` table. A batch buffers into sections and is assembled at apply time, because nft wants a document and because callers emit in a different order than the ruleset needs (jails are added last but must match first). One `nft -f` swaps the whole table after `nft -c -f` validates it, so there is no fail-open window and nothing half-applies. Dynamic sets render from source-of-truth files (fw_set_src) so a table replace cannot lose their contents; fw_set_replace does a live flush+refill in one transaction for the paths that must not rebuild everything. fw_legacy_teardown retires any iptables ruleset, which is mandatory because iptables is the nft shim and would otherwise keep being evaluated.

ssh_shell_jail.description: SSH/SFTP access control: the 3-tier access ladder — nologin (SFTP-only chroot, the default) · jailbash (bubblewrap-sandboxed interactive shell, opt-in) · bash (unconfined). #223 was the baseline check; the non-SFTP hardening landed in #412 (Story 1); the SFTP transport/chroot was rebuilt on pam_namespace in #413 (Story 2). See docs branch jail-chroot-story{1,2}-plan.md.
ssh_shell_jail.jailbash: share/bubblewrap/jailbash (moved from install/common/bubblewrap; deployed to /usr/sbin/jailbash by h-add-sys-ssh-jail) — bwrap wrapper run as the jailbash login shell: reuses host /usr read-only but with private /tmp,/home,/var,/run and stub passwd/group, --unshare-all (incl. pid → fresh /proc) --share-net. NEAR-VERBATIM UPSTREAM (origin/upstream/hestiacp) — tracked for drift (the #412 5-bind re-sync of zoneinfo/php/ca-certificates/i18n + /etc/php, lost behind `--tmpfs /usr/share`, was a chance find; a CI drift-gate is planned). Registered as a login shell in /etc/shells by h-add-sys-ssh-jail. NOTE: --share-net means 127.0.0.1 inside the jail is the HOST loopback (a jailbash user reaches host-bound services: redis:6379, webmail FPM :8090/:8091, panel, adminer) — an open isolation question tracked in Story 1 verification, not yet closed.
ssh_shell_jail.apparmor_userns_quirk: On Ubuntu 24.04+/kernels with apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, unprivileged user namespaces are blocked and bwrap fails without the `bwrap-userns-restrict` AppArmor profile (source: share/bubblewrap/bwrap-userns-restrict, deployed to /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap-userns-restrict by h-add-sys-ssh-jail). That profile is installed ONLY when /etc/apparmor.d/abi/4.0 exists (the artefact-based guard, NOT an OS-version flag). Keep this rationale verbatim — hard-won.
ssh_shell_jail.shell_allowlist: func/main.sh HESTIA_SHELL_ALLOWLIST + list_allowed_shells (#412): the single curated source (nologin/jailbash/bash/sh ∩ /etc/shells, nologin guaranteed) shared by is_format_valid_shell (hard validator) AND h-list-sys-shells (the panel dropdown source for web/edit/user + web/{add,edit}/package). Dropped from upstream: rssh (gone from Debian, silently degrades to nologin), screen/tmux (useless as login shell), dash/rbash. The validator is genuinely hard (not a UI-only filter): h-change-user-shell gates every genuine change through it, EXCEPT re-asserting the user's current shell (in-allowlist OR ==current — so a legacy off-list shell a restore left in place can be re-set, but no new off-list shell slips in). rebuild.sh sets the shell straight from /etc/shells (bypasses the validator) so restore stays tolerant; the user/package editors render an existing off-allowlist shell as a selected "(current)" option so an unchanged save never resets it. FTP_SHELL (domain-FTP sub-accounts, h-add-web-domain-ftp/rebuild.sh) is a SECOND shell source that bypasses both panel and validator → Story 2.
ssh_shell_jail.allowusers: func/main.sh manage_sshd_allowusers add|del <user> — co-maintains an AllowUsers login allowlist in /etc/ssh/sshd_config; installer seeds it commented/inert. Panel users hooked in #412 (h-add-user/h-delete-user/rebuild_user); domain-FTP sub-accounts hooked in #413 (h-add-web-domain-ftp/h-delete-web-domain-ftp). See func_libraries.file_roles.main.sh for the full contract.
ssh_shell_jail.sftp_jail: pam_namespace SFTP jail (#413), replacing the old /srv/jail systemd bind-mount machinery. Per session, pam_namespace mounts a private tmpfs on /run/hestia/jail (from share/tmpfiles.d/hestia-jail.conf) and runs share/security/hestia-jail.init INSIDE the new mount namespace, as root, BEFORE sshd chroots: it builds the jail at the FIDELITY path (/run/hestia/jail/$user/<real-home>, from getent passwd) and bind-mounts the real home there — so ONE generic rule serves both panel users (home /home/$user) and domain-FTP sub-accounts (user-owned home deep under web/$domain, which native chroot cannot handle). fail-closed rides on sshd's own safely_chroot() (aborts if any chroot component is not root-owned or is group/other-writable): the fresh tmpfs root is 1777, the init builds everything while it is still 1777 and `chmod 755` on the root is the LAST action, so any failure leaves it 1777 → session refused (pam_namespace IGNORES the init exit code, so this is the real gate). Scope: the sftp-jailed group is BOTH the sshd chroot selector (one static `Match Group sftp-jailed` block) AND the PAM scope (`session [success=1 default=ignore] pam_succeed_if.so user notingroup sftp-jailed` before pam_namespace, so only members build a jail — non-members log in unchanged). Per user this is just group membership (add_chroot_jail=usermod -aG, delete_chroot_jail=gpasswd -d). No /home ownership flip (chroot root is root-owned in the tmpfs; the home keeps user ownership). No persistent state: no /srv/jail, no .mount units, no @reboot cron, no growing Match User list; /run/hestia/jail is tmpfs → self-heals on reboot via tmpfiles.d. Verified live on OpenSSH 9.2/9.6/10.0/10.2 (deb12/ub24/deb13/ub26), userns restriction active on ub26 with NO unprivileged userns/bwrap involved.
ssh_shell_jail.sftp_jail_quirks: Hard-won, non-obvious, expensive to rediscover — keep verbatim (same category as apparmor_userns_quirk): (1) pam_namespace IGNORES the iscript's exit code — fail-closed cannot ride on `exit 1`; it rides on sshd's safely_chroot() via the chmod-755-as-LAST-action on the still-1777 tmpfs root (any earlier failure leaves it world-writable → refused). (2) hestia-jail.init is a pam_namespace CALLBACK, never a standalone script: run by hand (even under `unshare -m`) it lacks slave-propagation, so `mount --bind` LEAKS the bind onto the host. Guarded by `mountpoint -q $polydir` (pam_namespace mounts the per-session tmpfs on the polydir before calling the iscript, so it is a mountpoint only in the real path; PAM_USER is NOT exported to the iscript, so it is not a usable discriminator — the mountpoint is). (3) A SKIPPED build (pam_namespace not firing at all) is still fail-closed: ChrootDirectory is always /run/hestia/jail/%u (never /home/%u), and that per-user dir exists only inside the per-session tmpfs → no build → missing dir → sshd refuses; it cannot resolve to the real home. (4) ForceCommand internal-sftp in the Match Group block forces SFTP even for a jailed user who has a real login shell (ssh-not-sftp → 'sftp connections only', no shell).

file_manager.description: Web file manager (#419 rebuild — replaces the old FileGator + SFTP-loopback connector). A per-customer php-fpm pool runs the app AS the customer, so the kernel UID is the file-access boundary (no connector, no keys, no crypto). Reached only via Panel-Caddy /fm/ → forward_auth → a private loopback listener → the customer pool. Baseline #218, integration concept #419. The app is a maintained fork of TinyFileManager 2.6 (single-file PHP), put on a diet: no external CDN — Bootstrap-CSS + a combined PrismJS build are vendored under share/filemanager/fm/assets/, FontAwesome (FA7) + (where needed) the panel's own assets are referenced same-origin; jQuery/Bootstrap-JS/DataTables/Dropzone/Ace/highlight.js are replaced by vanilla JS + a tiny Bootstrap-compatible modal/dropdown/tab shim, a native chunked uploader, native table filter/sort, and a Prism-overlay code editor (highlighting + line numbers, no preview). Vendoring is tracked in VENDORED.json (tinyfilemanager/prismjs/bootstrap-css) with upstream/* snapshot branches. Security note: the FM is SAME-ORIGIN with the panel (:8083/fm/), so any path that emits customer bytes is a panel-origin XSS surface — the ?media= handler therefore sets Content-Type ONLY from a server-side extension allowlist (never finfo/client), forces everything else (incl. SVG) to application/octet-stream + attachment, and always sends X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff + CSP default-src 'none'; sandbox; the third-party Google/MS doc-viewer iframes were removed (URL leak + broken off-box). Caddy drops all inbound X-Hestia-* (request_header -X-Hestia-*) before re-setting the trusted ones — the §7.2 invariant made structural. The FA4→FA7 icon remap covers the icons TFM actually references (fewer than a raw 1:1 of every upstream FA4 name; duplicates/unused dropped).
file_manager.two_hop: Caddy never talks to a customer FPM pool directly: an FPM socket is an interpreter (the client picks SCRIPT_FILENAME = code exec as the pool user), and www-data already has that reach over every customer pool (capability-neutral) whereas caddy (the phpMyAdmin/Roundcube user) does not — so /fm/ goes Caddy → nginx/apache private listener (as www-data) → the fm-<user> pool. nginx fronts it whenever it fronts the stack (nginx-only or nginx+apache); apache only in apache-only.
file_manager.auth: web/fm-auth.php is the ONLY authorization stop (the app runs with its own login disabled — the process is the tenant). Caddy /fm/* forward_auth → fm-auth.php (panel FPM, as hestia): a valid panel session → returns X-Hestia-User = the effective user (look/impersonation else session user). The 'enabled?' gate is the pool SOCKET's existence /run/hestia/fm/<user>.sock (a cheap stat — hestia CANNOT read /etc/hestia which is 700 root:root, so it does NOT read the FILE_MANAGER flag directly), which is the structural truth (no pool → no vhost → fail-closed).
file_manager.secret_invariant: The §7.2 invariant (guarded by the D6 smoke test): Caddy OVERWRITES two headers, never passing a client value — Host = fm-<user>.local (from the forward_auth response, selects the customer vhost) and X-Hestia-FM-Auth = the shared secret (/etc/hestia/conf/.filemanager.key, root:root 0600, baked into the caddy route at deploy time so caddy never reads the file). The private listener 403s without the secret and binds 127.0.0.1:FILE_MANAGER_PORT (8092) only.
file_manager.lifecycle: h-add-sys-filemanager deploys shared read-only code to /usr/share/filemanager/fm, generates the secret + tmpfiles socket dir + Caddy route, and reactivates saved per-user flags; h-delete-sys-filemanager reverses it but KEEPS per-user FILE_MANAGER flags (saved state, re-add reactivates). Per customer, h-add/delete-user-filemanager add/remove the pool (runs as the customer, pm=ondemand) + private vhost + FILE_MANAGER flag. rebuild_user (func/rebuild.sh) re-creates the pool+vhost for FILE_MANAGER=yes users — restore bypasses h-add-user-filemanager, so without it a restored user keeps the flag+menu but has no working FM (same lockout class as the AllowUsers fix 62eb1ca). h-add-user-filemanager waits for the pool socket before returning (no enable-time 403 race). Panel menu: h-list-user exposes the per-user FILE_MANAGER flag; top_panel() surfaces the EFFECTIVE (impersonation-aware) user's flag as $_SESSION['USER_FILE_MANAGER'] and web/templates/includes/panel.php gates the 'File manager' entry on it === 'yes' (its own key — never mixes with the legacy system-wide FileGator FILE_MANAGER).
file_manager.quirks: Hard-won, keep verbatim: (1) FILE_MANAGER must NOT be the last user.conf line — update_user_value deletes+reinserts by line number and a last-line key fails to reinsert (the address lands past EOF) and vanishes on the first toggle; it is inserted before TIME + seeded in rebuild's default block + registered in syshealth known_keys (where LOGIN_*/RATE_LIMIT are also still missing — pre-existing). (2) Stock TinyFileManager is NOT integration-ready — Phase-2 patches: P2 ($use_auth=false → trust forward_auth, else it shows its own login), P3 (root from getenv('FM_ROOT'), NOT $_SERVER['DOCUMENT_ROOT'] which is /usr/share/filemanager, outside open_basedir → TFM echoes 'Root path not found'), P-selfurl (FM_SELF_URL/FM_ROOT_URL prepend HTTP_HOST = the internal routing host fm-<user>.local which the browser cannot resolve → make them relative). (3) FM app errors: the pool sets catch_workers_output=yes + log_errors=on, so they land in the php-fpm log tagged [pool fm-<user>]; TFM's own 'Root path' error is echoed to the page, not logged.

upstream_ref.share/clamav/: install/deb/clamav/clamd.conf moved here (#123; deployed by h-add-sys-clamav — was orphaned; hardened LocalSocketMode 666→660 + LogVerbose off) plus two NEW curated files: socket-hardening.conf (systemd .socket drop-in) and apparmor-local. ClamAV is the antivirus analogue of rspamd: the exim `.ifdef CLAMD` block (av_scanner=clamd: + per-domain antivirus ACL + `deny malware=*/defer_ok`) was fully shipped but inert (macro commented). h-add-sys-clamav sets ANTIVIRUS_SYSTEM=clamav and arms the CLAMD macro ONLY after clamd answers on the socket (clamdscan --ping) — DB-download timeout leaves it OFF + honest WARN, because `defer_ok` is FAIL-OPEN (dead clamd → mail accepted UNSCANNED, not deferred), so an armed-but-blind macro would silently pass mail. THREE non-obvious wiring facts, all found in live testing: (1) BIDIRECTIONAL group membership — exim joins clamav (write the socket) AND clamav joins Debian-exim (READ /var/spool/exim4/scan, 0750 exim:exim); the second is load-bearing, without it clamd errors 'Permission denied' on the spool → fail-open passes mail unscanned. (2) The 660 socket is enforced by socket-hardening.conf (SocketMode=0660), NOT clamd.conf's LocalSocketMode — clamd is socket-activated so the clamav-daemon.socket unit owns the live /run/clamav/clamd.ctl mode (default 0666); the add script installs the drop-in + `systemctl restart clamav-daemon.socket`, and restarts the daemon (not enable --now) so it re-forks with the new group + socket. (3) apparmor-local re-asserts `/var/spool/exim4/** r,` into the clamd profile's local hook — the stock usr.sbin.clamd profile already grants it (0 denials on all 4 distros), this is defensive for a stricter base install; guarded on the profile file + `apparmor_parser … || true`, so a no-AppArmor host installs fine and the exim chain still scans (it relies on unix group perms, not AppArmor). Delete = saved-state (per-domain flags kept, restored on reinstall); the virus DB is moved aside across the purge and restored (apt purge clamav-freshclam wipes /var/lib/clamav) unless PURGE_DATA=yes, and the add script chowns it back to clamav in case the purge/reinstall re-allocated the uid. list_mail.php AV/spam columns now gate on ANTIVIRUS_SYSTEM/ANTISPAM_SYSTEM (neutral dash when the addon is gone).

panel_php_service.description: Dedicated PHP-FPM service for the HestiaRE panel. Runs as hestia-php.service using Sury php8.3-fpm binary with an isolated pool. Replaces compiled hestia-php package.
panel_php_service.confd_isolation: The panel FPM runs with PHP_INI_SCAN_DIR=/etc/php/hestia/fpm/conf.d (set in hestia-php-fpm) so it loads a curated extension set independent of the customer version's conf.d (#272). hestia-php-confd rebuilds it from the pinned version's mods-available; called by install_panel, h-change-sys-panel-php, and migrate_data_layout. Wrapper falls back to the default scan dir if unbuilt. APP→EXTENSION COUPLING (the reason the set is what it is): EVERY app on this single FPM master shares this one fpm conf.d — (1) panel UI web/, (2) phpMyAdmin+Adminer, (3) webmail Roundcube+SnappyMail (#205). hestia-php-confd curates them as fpm_* / fpm_apps_* / fpm_webmail_* respectively. AUDIT RULE: before dropping any extension grep all three app groups, not just the panel/DB tools — a 2026-07 audit dropped `dom` after checking only panel+phpMyAdmin+Adminer and 500'd every Roundcube page (Roundcube's html.php renders via DOMDocument). Non-obvious members: intl (webmail IDN), phar (SnappyMail plugins), dom (Roundcube). Excluded on purpose: imagick/imap/ldap/soap/bcmath/apcu (customer-app extensions). sodium is compiled-in on Sury (no mods-available .ini).
panel_php_service.version_indirection: The panel PHP version is the single source of truth in /etc/php/hestia/php-version (written by h-install-hestia, read by the hestia-php / hestia-php-fpm wrappers). h-change-sys-panel-php (#272) rewrites it + restarts hestia-php; h-delete-web-php refuses to remove the pinned version. Distinct from h-change-sys-php (default web PHP).

stages.install_base: APT repos (Sury always; MariaDB only for an external-repo version), base packages, system users, SSH hardening (Subsystem internal-sftp, LoginGraceTime 1m, DebianBanner no, and a commented #AllowUsers allowlist seed co-maintained by manage_sshd_allowusers, #412), NTP, /proc hardening via proc_hardening_apply (func/helper.sh: hidepid persisted via the hestia-proc-hardening.service unit from share/security/systemd, replacing the @reboot cron; NOT fstab - the systemd fstab generator skips API filesystems so a /proc line there is inert; skipped in containers where the remount is refused, re-asserted on upgrade from migrate_data_layout). The unit resolves the procvis gid from /etc/group on every start rather than carrying an install-time value, so a deleted+recycled gid cannot silently exempt a foreign group; gid=0 when the group is absent, which is also how a stale exemption is withdrawn (a remount that merely omits gid keeps the old value). hidepid=invisible is required, not a preference: noaccess leaves foreign pids enumerable with their owners (156 vs 3 measured) AND still breaks rootless Docker. h-check-sys-smoke check_proc_hardening verifies the live mount, since failure is fail-open
stages.install_web: nginx + apache2 per WEB_SERVER with port model #247 (BOTH: nginx proxy 80/443 -> apache2 8080/8443; APACHE/NGINX alone: 80/443; Listen per IP via h-add-sys-ip, ports.conf emptied, mod_remoteip for client IP behind proxy), multi-PHP via COMPONENT_PHP_MULTIPHP_VERSIONS when sury_multi, web pool

stages.install_mail: exim4, dovecot (version-aware), rspamd (optional), webmailer roundcube/snappymail — only if COMPONENT_MAIL_BLOCK_PRESENT
stages.install_addons: proftpd (→ h-add-sys-proftpd) / docker / filemanager per components (#123)

web_botlimit.description: Server-native web bot rate-limiting, Layer B (#482) - a standalone subsystem, independent of CrowdSec and available on ANY web install (nginx-only, apache-only, both). Throttles bot families with native nginx limit_req / apache mod_qos and answers 429; humans are NEVER limited and malicious traffic stays CrowdSec's job (ban -> 403), so the two never overlap. Driven by an admin family table (share/botpolicy/botfamilies.conf seeded to /etc/hestia/botfamilies.conf, 8 curated families + 2 free slots, capped at 10 because each family costs two limit_req zones plus one more alternative in the per-request UA map). Per family: UA match + lenient/strict rate + enabled, plus conf-only advanced burst/nodelay. Per domain each family is off/lenient/strict via the web.conf BOTLIMIT field, rendered into a per-vhost fragment the templates include by glob (absent = no-op). nginx keys per family PER DOMAIN ($host:family, set inside the map VALUE so a non-bot UA still maps to "" and stays unlimited) - a busy customer's crawlers cannot 429 another customer out of a shared bucket; apache mod_qos counts per client IP. Default off/opt-in. KNOWN LIMITATION: families match on the spoofable User-Agent and Layer B does not verify it (no rDNS/IP check), so on a non-CrowdSec install a client faking a crawler UA can drain that family's bucket; on CrowdSec installs the good-actor whitelist verifies real crawlers by rDNS/IP. INVARIANT: the server config defines zones only for ENABLED families, so a fragment must never reference a gone/disabled one - nginx -t would fail and block the next reload for the whole box; the fragment renderer skips them, the apply command re-renders every throttled domain first, and deleting a family also strips it from every domain.
web_botlimit.core: func/botpolicy.sh (botpolicy_seed_families, botpolicy_render_nginx/_apache, botpolicy_apply, botpolicy_render_domain_fragment, botpolicy_render_all_fragments, botpolicy_purge_family, botpolicy_rate_to_qos)

web_botlimit.panel: the family table is inline on Server Settings (web/edit/server/, admin-only, 10 slots saved with the settings form: APPLY=no per row + a single apply at the end; placement provisional pending the panel overhaul) + the Bot Rate Limiting section in web/edit/web/ (per-domain off/lenient/strict for the admin-ENABLED families, customer-editable and also settable by an admin while impersonating; only the family table stays admin-only. A customer cannot reach another tenant: the panel passes the effective session user and the CLI validates the domain against that user's own object file. Disabled families and unused slots never appear). h-list-web-domain exposes BOTLIMIT so the panel can see a domain's own levels.

crowdsec.description: CrowdSec integration (#186), nginx-front only, in four layers. Layer A (L7): own dependency-free LuaJIT ban-bouncer that queries the local LAPI live and answers 403; rendered per web model + a per-domain fragment. L3: own cscli->ipset feeder (bin/h-update-firewall-crowdsec, timer-driven) fills a hestia-crowdsec DROP chain via h-update-firewall - the OS crowdsec-firewall-bouncer 0.0.25 is fleet-unusable (nil-panics in nftablesConfig). The feeder DENYLISTS scenario tokens so only web-tier bans normally reach the firewall; the auth families (ssh/ftp/mail/db) are denied only while fail2ban is present (FIREWALL_EXTENSION) - in the crowdsec-only model they reach L3 too (best-effort SSH/web enforcement, #498), while req-limit stays denied in every model so a Layer-B 429 never escalates. Fleet-mesh: peer-mesh shared blocklist, no central LAPI - each box publishes its own local bans and imports the union of its peers' as L7-only mesh bans (origin cscli-import, scenario hestia-mesh:<peer>); enforcement falls out for free (the L7 bouncer sees imported decisions, the L3 feeder filters origin==crowdsec). Packaged as a removable addon (#123). The LAPI is loopback-only (127.0.0.1:8054) throughout. Layer-B bot rate-limiting was decoupled into its own always-available subsystem (func/botpolicy.sh, #482) - CrowdSec bans, botpolicy throttles, and the two never overlap. crowdsec_apply removes crowdsecurity/nginx-req-limit-exceeded on purpose: it would escalate our own 429s into bans.
crowdsec.core: func/crowdsec.sh (engine install, Layer-A bouncer + per-model/per-domain rendering), func/crowdsec-mesh.sh (peering + pull transport helpers)
crowdsec.model: Three models, asked once in the wizard as CROWDSEC_MODE and switchable at runtime with h-change-sys-crowdsec-mode (#494): capi = central community blocklist + telemetry; local = self-hosted engine only; mesh = local plus the peer exchange, so mesh always disables the CAPI online_client. The LIVE model is derived from artefacts (is online_client commented out? does /etc/hestia/crowdsec/mesh.conf exist?) via crowdsec_current_mode - COMPONENT_CROWDSEC_MODE in install.conf is the install recipe, not live state. crowdsec_enable_capi is the inverse of crowdsec_disable_capi and rolls back to local if enrolment fails, because cscli capi register (1.4.x) loads the credentials file before writing it and so needs both an uncommented online_client AND an existing (possibly empty) file.
crowdsec.mesh_transport: Authenticated pull over the panel port (#485): web/mesh-decisions.php serves this box's published ban list behind a per-peer bearer token; web/mesh-pair.php completes a pairing that the peer initiated with a one-time code minted here. A pairing therefore needs an admin on BOTH boxes (initiating needs root/admin there, minting the code needs root/admin here) and /mesh-pair.php is a plain 404 while no code is live. TLS is pinned per peer (SPKI, TOFU at pairing) since panel certs are usually self-signed; each side installs an IP-scoped ACCEPT rule for the other on the panel port (never narrowing :8083 to peers-only). Secrets never ride in argv (/proc is world-readable): the panel hands payloads over in 0600 files under /run/hestia/mesh/in, curl reads tokens from a 0600 config, and only token HASHES are staged for the panel to compare (it runs as hestia and cannot read /etc/hestia).
crowdsec.config: /etc/hestia/crowdsec/{mesh.conf,peers.conf,pairing.conf} (root 0600; mesh.conf presence = mesh on), /run/hestia/mesh/{published.json,tokens,in} (panel-readable staging, tmpfiles.d + refilled by the timer)
crowdsec.panel: web/list/firewall/mesh/ + web/add/firewall/mesh/ + web/delete/firewall/mesh/ + web/generate/mesh-pairing/ (admin-only Fleet Mesh page: peers, shared-ban counts, generate/enter a pairing code)
crowdsec.timers: hestia-crowdsec-l3.timer (ipset feeder), hestia-crowdsec-mesh.timer (publish + pull + swap-import; the import is skipped while the union is unchanged and the decisions' TTL is still fresh)
crowdsec.smoke_guards: bin/h-check-sys-smoke (L3 + mesh timer checks, both artefact-gated)
crowdsec.no_symlink: new h-* commands, no v-* symlink

firewall.description: Host firewall, rebuilt on nftables in #495. func/firewall.sh is the sole owner of backend syntax and bin/h-update-firewall the sole full-ruleset writer: it renders one inet hestia table and applies it as a single atomic nft -f document, validated with nft -c -f first. Base chains carry hook + priority so foreign tables (fail2ban's own, a future bouncer's) coexist instead of fighting over INPUT. Sets render from their source files rather than from the live set, so a wholesale table replace cannot lose contents. iptables is xtables-nft-multi on all four targets, which means a leftover iptables ruleset is STILL EVALUATED by the same kernel backend - legacy teardown is mandatory, not housekeeping. inet covers v4 and v6 and loads on a host with no IPv6 configured, which is what lays the v6 groundwork without presupposing it.
firewall.object_model: /etc/hestia/firewall/{rules.conf,chains.conf,banlist.conf,ipset.conf,excludes.conf,crowdsec.conf,custom.sh} - abstract and renderer-independent, which is why the nftables migration keeps it and replaces only the marshalling. custom.sh is an operator escape hatch bashed after every apply. excludes.conf is the whitelist and is currently READ at exactly one place (h-add-firewall-ban, where it suppresses new bans) and WRITTEN BY NOTHING - no command, no panel page, no shipped default.
firewall.persistence: iptables-save (with a sed that strips individual fail2ban ban lines, since bans are replayed from banlist.conf instead) to /etc/iptables.rules, plus an inline-generated hestia-iptables.service whose ExecStartPre=- provisions the ipsets. iptables-restore is atomic PER TABLE, so one rule matching a set that failed to load rejects the whole filter table and the box boots with policy ACCEPT - and the dash prefix means the provisioning failure is ignored. h-check-sys-smoke guards both halves of that (check_firewall_closed, check_firewall_sets_bootable).
firewall.blocklists: Lists referenced from a normal rule as IP='ipset:<name>'; the operator picks the ACTION, so a list is advisory rather than implicitly a DROP. Sources come from share/firewall/blocklists.conf (FireHOL L1/L2, Spamhaus DROP, Blocklist.de), read by the panel picker, so adding one is a data change (#481) - it replaced a shipped preset pointing at install/common/firewall/ipset/blacklist.sh, a path dissolved with the install/ tree in #119, which failed on the minimum-size check with a misleading error. Refresh runs off hestia-blocklist.timer (Persistent=true, RandomizedDelaySec=30min) rather than queue/daily.pipe, with the interval set by h-change-sys-blocklist-interval. nft interval sets carry auto-merge, so overlapping CIDRs collapse on load (1665 Spamhaus CIDRs -> 1509 elements) and the live element count will not match the source count. #510 tracks a dynamic picker with per-list size and age.
firewall.core: func/firewall.sh is the renderer library (#495); every backend call in bin/ and func/ goes through it - a repo-wide sweep for direct iptables invocation outside that file returns nothing.
firewall.smoke_guards: bin/h-check-sys-smoke: check_firewall_closed (INPUT policy must be DROP while FIREWALL_SYSTEM is set) and check_firewall_sets_bootable (every --match-set in the PERSISTED ruleset must have a boot provisioning path). The second reads the saved file on purpose - the kernel refuses --match-set for a nonexistent set, so a live dangling reference cannot exist and checking for one would always pass.
firewall.config_keys: FIREWALL_SYSTEM (nftables|empty - the VALUE changed in #495; renaming it left six sites comparing against the old 'iptables' literal, one of which let the panel destroy the live ruleset) gates every h-*-firewall* command via is_system_enabled and has h-add-sys-firewall/h-delete-sys-firewall plus a panel toggle. FIREWALL_EXTENSION (fail2ban|empty) is written ONLY by the installer and never cleared, so fail2ban cannot be turned off - see the fail2ban component and #497.
firewall.panel: web/{list,add,edit,delete,bulk,move,suspend,unsuspend}/firewall/ - rules, banlist, whitelist (exclude/), jail status (jail/), ipset, mesh. The whitelist page is NOT gated on FIREWALL_EXTENSION: it renders as a firewall accept and works without fail2ban, which is also what makes it the way back in after a lockout.
firewall.roadmap: Umbrella #481 (also Stage 0: the reference captures under firewall-captures/ on the docs branch are the equivalence reference for the renderer swap). #495 nftables renderer + native sets, #496 fail2ban, #497 fail2ban as an addon, #498 model matrix. Plans: firewall-roadmap.md + firewall-subsystem-analysis.md + nftables-migration-plan.md on the docs branch. Known defects D1-D8 are catalogued in the analysis doc.

fail2ban.description: Brute-force protection, wired as a CLIENT of the hestia firewall rather than as an independent writer: share/fail2ban/action.d/hestia.conf maps actionstart/stop/ban/unban onto h-add/delete-firewall-chain and h-add/delete-firewall-ban, so bans land in banlist.conf AND in the live fail2ban-<CHAIN> chain and therefore survive a full h-update-firewall rebuild. That client model is the reason to keep owning the ban action rather than adopting fail2ban's native nftables banaction, which would bypass the banlist, the panel and rebuild-survival alike.
fail2ban.config_install: fail2ban_apply in func/fail2ban.sh is the single implementation of "a configured fail2ban", shared by the installer and (later) the addon commands. It copies the WHOLE share/fail2ban tree through a staging dir: enumerating the files individually is what once left out action.d/hestia.conf and made every jail using action = hestia[...] unstartable with smoke still green (D1, fixed in #502). Our jails live in jail.d/hestia.local, never in jail.local, which is left to the admin - fail2ban reads jail.conf -> jail.d/*.conf -> jail.local -> jail.d/*.local, so ours is read last and wins. The distro [sshd] jail is disabled from our own config rather than by deleting jail.d/defaults-debian.conf: that is a dpkg conffile, so rm -f is undone by the next package update.
fail2ban.jails: share/fail2ban/jail.local ships ssh, exim, dovecot, proftpd, hestia-panel, phpmyadmin, the four web-log jails (web-botsearch, web-badactor, web-exploit, web-authprobe), roundcube-auth, snappymail-auth and recidive. The web-* four are the L7 layer (#531): web-botsearch bans 404-enumeration on the botsearch vocabulary (rate, maxretry 10), web-badactor bans secret/config file-discovery paths, web-exploit bans traversal/RCE/appliance payloads (both status-agnostic, maxretry 2), web-authprobe bans repeated 401 (401-only; maxretry 20 because it counts per source IP AGGREGATED across all vhosts, not per domain). All L7 jails are signature/behaviour based, never rate - that is Layer B's job (func/botpolicy.sh) and its 429s must never escalate to a ban. They are gated together as one set (func/fail2ban.sh F2B_WEB_JAILS): fail2ban_gate_web_jail repoints their logpath at the configured web system, fail2ban_watch_domain addlogpath/dellogpath's each domain across all of them, and a per-filter smoke canary (check_fail2ban_web_signatures via fail2ban-regex) pins match+reject. Mail jails are gated on the mail model, proftpd on FTP_SYSTEM, the web jails on WEB_SYSTEM, and the two webmail jails on WEBMAIL_SYSTEM (each client independently) - a jail whose logpath does not exist never fires and says so only in fail2ban's own log. No mysqld jail on purpose: 3306 is not in the shipped ruleset, so it is loopback-only and h-add-firewall-ban would refuse to ban what could reach it. recidive covers ports 1:65535 and is what gives whole-box escalation - CrowdSec has no analogue today. Whitelisting is NOT configured here: h-add-firewall-exclude maintains it and mirrors it into jail.d/hestia-zz-whitelist.local.
fail2ban.hazards: fail2ban expands a logpath GLOB once, when the jail starts, and never again - a web domain added later is simply not watched, silently, until the daemon restarts. So h-add-web-domain, h-delete-web-domain, h-change-web-domain-name and rebuild_web_domain_conf all call fail2ban_watch_domain, which uses addlogpath/dellogpath to touch just that jail's file list without a reload. The web jail deliberately does NOT act on the rate limiter's 429s: Layer B (nginx limit_req / apache mod_qos) throttles bots itself and its verdicts must not escalate into firewall bans. Historic, all fixed: actionstop wiping the banlist and the multiport delete asymmetry (D4, #502), the dead unban grep (D6, withdrawn - the action really is named hestia-<CHAIN>), IPv4-only ban validation (D7, #506).
fail2ban.modularity: A removable addon like proftpd/clamav/crowdsec (#497): h-add-sys-fail2ban installs the package, sets FIREWALL_EXTENSION and runs the shared fail2ban_apply; h-delete-sys-fail2ban runs fail2ban_teardown (stop daemon, drop every chain from chains.conf via h-delete-firewall-chain, remove our config), clears FIREWALL_EXTENSION, re-renders the ruleset and purges the package. The three-way boolean has one live truth per layer, flipped together: COMPONENT_ADDON_FAIL2BAN (install.conf) gates the smoke block, FIREWALL_EXTENSION (hestia.conf) gates runtime/renderer/panel/services, $_SESSION mirrors it for the panel. add refuses without FIREWALL_SYSTEM active (the ban action needs a ruleset); no saved state - our config re-renders from share/, the admin's jail.local is untouched. Panel toggle sits next to the firewall one in edit/server.
fail2ban.demarcation_with_crowdsec: The distro crowdsec package's own postinst installs crowdsecurity/linux + crowdsecurity/sshd and acquires /var/log/auth.log, so CrowdSec DOES detect SSH brute force. The L3 feeder's auth-family denylist keeps those decisions off L3 only WHILE fail2ban is present, so fail2ban owns SSH enforcement (~1s, cuts live connections) in the fail2ban and fail2ban+crowdsec models. In the crowdsec-only model (#498) fail2ban is gone and the feeder lets the auth families through to L3 - best-effort, ~45s latency, connections not cut. Mail still has no CrowdSec detection surface (no exim/dovecot collections), so crowdsec-only leaves mail brute force unprotected: a documented best-effort gap. The model is switched at runtime with h-change-sys-firewall-model, which derives the current model from the artefacts and orchestrates the two addon commands.
fail2ban.panel: web/list/firewall/banlist/ + add/delete/bulk, and web/list/firewall/jail/ for jail status (h-list-firewall-jail). The banlist merges fail2ban bans (banlist.conf) with CrowdSec local L3 decisions (h-list-firewall-crowdsec-ban, origin==crowdsec only) source-tagged, and unban routes by source (fail2ban -> h-delete-firewall-ban; crowdsec -> h-delete-firewall-crowdsec-ban); bulk value is source|ip|chain (a pipe, so IPv6 colons don't mis-split) (#527). The banlist button shows when FIREWALL_EXTENSION is set OR a CROWDSEC session signal is present (h-list-sys-config derives it from the L3 marker, so the button appears in the crowdsec-only model); jail status stays gated on FIREWALL_EXTENSION. The status page reports the jails our config enables UNION the jails fail2ban is running, so one that is configured but not running reads as stopped instead of vanishing - that gap is the reason it exists.
fail2ban.roadmap: Firewall roadmap Stages 0-4 delivered: #496 (fix + jail rework, whitelist page, jail-status view), #497 (removable addon), #498 (model matrix). The four models (none / fail2ban / fail2ban+crowdsec / crowdsec) are encoded by the two existing wizard checkboxes (crowdsec hidden on apache), switched at runtime by h-change-sys-firewall-model. crowdsec-only enforcement is best-effort (SSH/web to L3, mail detection still absent). Supersedes #236.
fail2ban.webmail_ip_chain: The webmail jails read the client IP through the panel-Caddy hop, which overwrites X-Forwarded-For to 127.0.0.1. Roundcube reads X-Real-IP (proxy_whitelist=127.0.0.1, log_logins), SnappyMail reads Client-IP (auth_logging, labs http_client_ip_check_proxy) - the webmail vhost sets both from $remote_addr so neither is forgeable. Roundcube logs the user field verbatim, so its filter anchors the real trailer to end-of-line and lets a greedy user match backtrack to the genuine IP block (username log-injection defence, verified). #515.

web_model_switch.description: Live web-serving model switch (#120): change a running server between nginx-only / both / apache-only (previously install-only). Four thin commands - h-add-sys-nginx, h-add-sys-apache2, h-delete-sys-nginx, h-delete-sys-apache2 - over one shared core in func/web-model.sh; the model is DERIVED from the configured component set (WEB_SYSTEM/PROXY_SYSTEM in hestia.conf, never dpkg). Apply order: acquire the exclusive freeze lock -> durable snapshot + crash sentinel -> configure_apache2 (if target uses apache) -> flip keyset (change + clear) -> mod_remoteip toggle (enable for both incl. NAT IPs, disable otherwise) -> rebuild per-IP + web + webmail -> clean old-model artifacts -> validate (nginx -t / apache2ctl configtest + inventory assertion) -> stop the departing server, then enable+restart the target's servers (port handover). Explicit rollback (restore snapshot + re-start/enable) on any failure; --recover restores from an interrupted run's sentinel snapshot. The freeze: h-restart-web/-proxy/-service defer, 47 web/mail-vhost mutators + the LE renewal acquire the lock (bounded + reentrant via HESTIA_WEB_LOCK_HELD), apache logrotate skips its reload while held. Backups carry a WEB_SYSTEM/PROXY_SYSTEM marker (backup.conf + hestia/web-system in the archive); restore prints visible template-downgrade + cross-model warnings. Enforced by three h-check-sys-smoke guards (lock coverage, pre-check coverage, stale-sentinel).
web_model_switch.backup_restore: bin/h-backup-user (model marker), bin/h-restore-user (visible warnings + cross-model banner)
web_model_switch.no_symlink: new h-* commands, no v-* symlink

web_switches.description: Per-domain switches replacing selectable templates (#219): admin suspension + customer offline render from share/web/suspend/{admin,offline}/ (nginx/proxy/apache2 tpl+stpl, all three web models share one path via WEBTPL_OVERRIDE in prepare_web_domain_values); proxy caching writes a fragment into the domain's nginx.location.d/ (read inside location / of the default proxy vhost) plus one zone file per domain under /etc/nginx/conf.d/cache-zone.<domain>.conf.
web_switches.render: func/domain.sh prepare_web_domain_values + add_web_config (WEBTPL_OVERRIDE, missing-template guard with skip tally)
web_switches.http3: #613 - a per-domain switch, not a template variant. quic listen + Alt-Svc go into nginx.ssl.conf_http3, picked up by the merged SSL block's generic nginx.ssl.conf_* glob (no template/renderer change). Gate (func/domain.sh nginx_has_http3): SSL + nginx front + nginx --with-http_v3_module (deb12/ub24 OS nginx lacks it). Plain quic, no reuseport. h-change-web-domain-ip re-emits the fragment (it carries the IP, is not a .conf); restore drops it when the target nginx cannot do http3.
web_switches.flags: web.conf OFFLINE / PROXY_CACHE / PROXY_CACHE_DURATION / HTTP3 - registered in syshealth_known_keys web and carried through both restore field lists
web_switches.guards: h-check-sys-smoke: check_web_cache_zones (flag without zone), check_vhost_nonempty (0-byte vhost)
web_switches.panel: web/edit/web/ - offline checkbox in the main form, proxy-cache block next to the FastCGI one (PROXY_SYSTEM=nginx only), HTTP/3 checkbox in the SSL section gated on session WEB_HTTP3 (computed by h-list-sys-config from nginx -V, folded into the session by inc/main.php) + an nginx front
web_switches.legacy_mapping: func/domain.sh accept_web_template + map_legacy_template - every write (CLI, restore, package) passes through; known legacy values are mapped with their side effect (caching -> cache switch, wordpress*-http3 -> base template + http3 switch), unknown ones error on the CLI and fall back on restore. Guard: check_web_templates_resolvable.
